[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, um thanks for joining, I'll kick off the call, this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya and Ethan. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Sarah: good thanks, morning actually for us. excited to get started.
[00:15] Tom: yeah thanks, appreciate you squeezing this in.
[00:18] Priya: great, quick agenda: intro, goals for pilot, infra questions, security/compliance, timeline and next steps. we'll keep it to about 45, 50 min.
[00:28] Jordan: quick rundowns, pinecrest — you told us you're trying to add summarization and clinical note generation across outpatient clinics, main concerns were data residency, latency for clinician workflows, and of course audit logs. is that still accurate?
[00:39] Sarah: yep that's right. low latency is important, esp during charting, also can't have PHI leave our VPC ideally.
[00:47] Alicia: also we need role-based access, and SSO integration with Okta.
[00:51] Ethan: great, so we typically recommend two paths: hosted API for fastest time-to-value, and Redwood Private (VPC) for customers who need data to stay in their network. for low latency and PHI constraints, Private or Dedicated in your cloud region tends to be the right fit.
[01:09] Tom: when you say Private, does that mean the control plane still touches redwood or is it fully customer-managed?
[01:14] Ethan: good q. our Private offering can be deployed with a private control plane — the control plane endpoints are reachable only from your VPC and we offer an on-prem package too. there is a customer-managed networking setup, and we integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management.
[01:29] Sarah: ok, and SOC 2, ISO — do you have certs and how do logs look?
[01:33] Priya: we're SOC 2 Type II certified, we can share the report under NDA. audit logs are accessible via the Redwood Console, you get detailed token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and we can stream logs to your SIEM.
[01:47] Sarah: great. are there any gotchas for egress charges or cross-region traffic if we run in our VPC?
[01:53] Ethan: depends on architecture; if you deploy dedicated capacity in your cloud region, most of the traffic remains internal and egress is minimal. if you need multi-region failover we can discuss routing policies, but it's configurable.
[02:07] Jordan: timeline question — what's realistic for a pilot?
[02:11] Priya: for Private with our standard template and your infra team's support, typical kickoff-to-pilot is 2-4 weeks; Dedicated or hosted can be even faster. for enterprise we usually plan a 4-week pilot with success metrics defined up front.
[02:24] Alicia: what's included in the pilot? are we given dedicated GPU instances or shared?
[02:29] Ethan: for pilot we can spin up a limited dedicated capacity pool or use a hosted trial with model pinning. for testing latency at scale we recommend a small Dedicated pool so you can validate throughput and token cost.
[02:43] Sarah: we will definitely want to measure p50/p95 latencies for 256 token responses and also evaluate hallucination rate on clinical prompts.
[02:51] Ethan: agreed. we'll help you run a set of eval prompts and tie quality regressions to prompt sets. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles to reduce cost while keeping quality.
[03:03] Tom: about network specifics — what's required on our side for VPC peering or private endpoints?
[03:09] Ethan: we provide a network checklist. basically you need outbound rules for control plane endpoints, we set up peering or private endpoints depending on cloud, and you'll need to open ports for the inference nodes. i'll send the checklist after this call.
[03:20] Tom: perfect. also curious about SSO — we use Okta and SCIM provisioning, how mature is your SAML and RBAC?
[03:28] Priya: we support SAML SSO with Okta and SCIM group sync, plus RBAC in the console so you can limit access to models, projects, billing. we'll share configuration docs.
[03:38] Sarah: any concerns around PHI, redaction, or storage? do you retain logs by default?
[03:44] Jordan: by default hosted retains logs for 30 days, but with Private we can configure retention policies per customer and support no-retention modes; all data at rest is encrypted and integrates with your KMS.
[03:55] Alicia: pricing — can you ballpark pilot costs for a small dedicated pool?
[03:59] Jordan: i'll share a pilot estimate in the pricing sheet; rough ballpark is X for a small committed pool but i'll put exact numbers in the doc.
[04:09] Sarah: ok great. who will be our day-to-day contact?
[04:12] Priya: i'll be your CSM during onboarding, Jordan handles contract and commercial, Ethan will be your SE for technical work.
[04:20] Tom: any references from healthcare customers we can speak with?
[04:23] Priya: yes we can provide references under NDA; we've done several engagements.
[04:28] Jordan: quick risk/objection check — we've heard customers worry about model drift/regressions after tuning, how do you monitor quality?
[04:35] Ethan: Redwood has eval runs tied to prompt sets and regression alerts. we can set up a continuous eval to alert on quality drops and auto-fallback to a previous model variant if needed.
[04:48] Sarah: sounds good. we'll need an internal sign-off from security and legal. can you share SOC 2 and network diagrams?
[04:54] Priya: yes — i'll send the security pack and a sample network diagram.
[04:58] Alicia: re: data residency — we need the inference nodes to run in us-west-2. is that supported?
[05:03] Ethan: yes we support deployments in us-west-2 and you can pin model versions and region.
[05:07] Jordan: to recap, immediate next steps: Jordan sends onboarding guide + pricing + SOW draft; Priya sends security docs and console invite; Ethan sends network checklist and schedules a deep-dive on VPC/peering. customer provides sample data and security contacts. any other items?
[05:25] Sarah: that covers it. can we get the deep-dive before the holidays?
[05:29] Ethan: we'll aim for Dec 22 for the technical deep-dive, if that works on your side.
[05:34] Tom: works for me.
